text:
sarah_support: Heads up — Acme's calls to an internal tool started failing after they renamed a tool in their private registry. They see TOOL_NOT_FOUND / schema mismatch during function/tool calling.

sarah_support: Errors from customer (excerpt):
```
HTTP 404 {"error":"tool_not_found","tool":"pricing_lookup","hint":"looked up alias 'pricing.lookup'"}
Function call payload: {"name":"pricingLookup","arguments":{...}}
```

mike_oncall: :eyes: Which deployment? Hosted or Private?

sarah_support: Private (customer VPC, us-west-2). They rolled a change last night to rename pricing_lookup -> pricing.lookup (dot rename). Retry didn't help.

julia_eng_runtime: On it. Can you dump gateway logs and the control plane sync status? Also what's the registry version reported by the customer's control plane?

sarah_support: Attached the gateway trace they sent:
```
[2025-11-28T03:02:11Z] ERROR gateway: tool lookup failed for 'pricingLookup' (normalized 'pricing.lookup') - cache miss, control-plane returned 404
[2025-11-28T03:02:12Z] INFO gateway: forwarded lookup to control-plane /tools/lookup?name=pricing.lookup
[2025-11-28T03:02:12Z] ERROR control-plane: registry entry not found
```

mike_oncall: I think registry sync job may have failed last night during deploy. Checking registry-sync job status now.

deploy-bot: registry-sync-ci (job id: js-9921) finished with status FAILED at 2025-11-28T03:12:04Z

mike_oncall: Failed job shows permission error writing to s3 snapshot: AccessDenied: PutObject denied for arn:aws:s3:::redwood-private-buckets/registry/snapshots/...

julia_eng_runtime: That would explain stale aliases in the private control plane. Short-term fix: manually push the missing registry snapshot to the customer's control plane and clear the gateway cache.

patrick_devex: Steps to push snapshot (manual):
1) ssh into control-plane host
2) upload snapshot: `aws s3 cp registry-snapshot-20251127.json s3://redwood-private-buckets/registry/snapshots/` (requires s3:PutObject)
3) trigger apply: `redwood controlplane apply-snapshot --file registry-snapshot-20251127.json`
4) clear gateway cache: `curl -X POST http://gateway.local/admin/cache/clear?prefix=tools:`

mike_oncall: I ran the apply-snapshot and cleared cache. Gateway now returns lookup success.

sarah_support: Customer confirmed — calls back to life. They ran test and now get 200 and function invoked.

sarah_support: Repro steps we logged for internal postmortem:
1) Customer renames tool locally `pricing_lookup` -> `pricing.lookup` and pushes to repo
2) CI triggers registry-sync to upload snapshot to s3
3) registry-sync job failed due to missing s3:PutObject permission in sync role
4) control plane never receives new snapshot and continues serving old registry
5) gateway cache keeps serving old name until cache cleared or control plane updated

julia_eng_runtime: Action items:
- [ ] Add s3:PutObject to registry-sync role (PR created: infra#2345)
- [ ] Add healthcheck/alert on registry-sync failures to paging for oncall
- [ ] Add a rollout step to fail if registry-sync fails

patrick_devex: Also adding a tenant-level health endpoint for registry_version so customers can detect mismatches early.

sarah_support: Closing for now. Customer ok. Follow-up tickets: INF-678 (perm fix), INF-679 (alert), DOCS-45 (doc on manual apply)

mike_oncall: :white_check_mark:
